audit.whatIsWrong: Every one of the seven full-layer phases[].side disagreed with the content win[] row beneath it: full read Talon/Talon/Talon/Talon/Skill/Skill/Talon, content read Karma/Karma/Karma/Karma/Talon/Talon/Karma.
audit.why: Content matches packet.levelChart and the 52.27% win rate: Karma outranges Talon 950 to 650 before 6, Talon takes over on Shadow Assault (100/80/60s), and Karma restabilises late as a peel engine.
audit.corrected: All seven sides moved onto the content values, with phases[4] and phases[5] whys rewritten to describe Talon winning those rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes were described without a single cooldown, and the level-6 flip was written as if nothing changed for Karma.
audit.why: Noxian Diplomacy 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s at 575 range, Rake 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s at 650, Assassin's Path has no cooldown of its own (the terrain does), Shadow Assault 100/80/60s.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, phases[4].why, ahead and content.early.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated, and the page instead taught a fabricated one: 'Talon needs wall proximity to threaten his E-vault burst combo' and 'vault-stun burst combos'. Talon has no stun, and his burst needs no wall.
audit.why: Riot text: Noxian Diplomacy leaps to a target outside melee range from 575; Rake is a 650 volley whose RETURN pass carries the bonus damage and slow; Assassin's Path only vaults terrain. Meanwhile Karma's W deals damage and REVEALS its target — but it needs a targetable unit, and Shadow Assault makes him Invisible, so the tether has to go on before he vanishes.
audit.corrected: Stated in dosFull[1].d, phases[4].why, spikes[0].text and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim, breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lintFindings).
audit.why: Titles promised one thing and the bodies explained another.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to their titles; cooldowns field now carries real numbers.

edits.before: No new ult — your 6 is a Mantra rank: faster cycles, bigger RQs. Press the early lead before scaling lanes wake up.
edits.after: Shadow Assault at 100s gives stealth and a converge on his landing spot — W cannot target an invisible Talon, so tether first.

edits.before: Blackfire/Luden's spike: RQ-W chains threaten kills outright. The lane is now or never — you fall off politely.
edits.after: His lethality spike plus Assassin's Path over any wall means he picks the angle; hold RE for the vault, not the wave.

edits.before: He dives a shield, a root tether, and a speed boost — annoying, but your damage falls off before his patience does.
edits.after: He vaults walls, leaps 575 with Noxian Diplomacy, and stealths at 6 — be far away and shielded for the moment he lands.

edits.before: Win early, frustrate the dives, and out-utility his snowball with shields and roots. Nothing here works through Rake — schedule your pattern around its cooldown.
edits.after: Win the first ten minutes, deny the flank, and out-utility his snowball with shields and roots. Nothing works through Rake's 9 seconds — schedule your forward steps around it.

edits.before: Talon wins by landing Rake, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Talon wins by opening with Rake's slow on the return pass, closing 575 with Noxian Diplomacy, and vaulting out before you answer.

edits.before: Ahead, sprint: RQ Talon off every wave, take plates with the lead, and W-root river picks — Karma leads are sprints, not marathons.
edits.after: Ahead, sprint: RQ him off the wave while Rake sits on its 9s, take plates, and W-root him whenever he steps up for a melee minion.

edits.before: Convert before the curve flips: plates, roams, river picks with W roots. Every minute past your spike is a minute rented from his.
edits.after: Convert before 6: plates, roams, W-root picks. Once Shadow Assault is up he chooses the fight, and every even minute after is his.

edits.before: - Talon Rake: matchup-defining — The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget RE shield-speed for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Rake (W) is 9s at rank 1 and 7s at rank 5, and the RETURN pass carries the bonus damage and the slow — stand off the return line. - Noxian Diplomacy is 8s and leaps from 575; Assassin's Path has no cooldown of its own, only the wall does.

edits.before: If Talon takes first blood, tighten up: Rake is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q and stay relevant through shields and roots.
edits.after: If Talon takes first blood, his Noxian Diplomacy leap already kills from 575 — farm near your tower with Q, stop standing beside walls, and spend Mantra on RE for whoever he flanks next.

edits.before: Carry early or enable late — RQ chips win lanes; RE + roots win the teamfights your early lead bought.
edits.after: Carry the level 1-4 window with RQ chip; after 6 you enable — RE the vault, W-root him off your carry.

edits.before: The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Rake is 9s at rank 1 and the return pass carries the slow — sidestep the return, then RQ him in the 9 seconds he has no poke.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, and on real windows RQ-W: the chunk plus tether-root turns a poke trade into a kill setup — E out before the answer.
edits.after: W reveals its target, so tether him as he steps in — once Shadow Assault turns him invisible there is nothing to click, and RE eats the burst.

edits.before: Talon spends Rake early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Talon leaves lane over walls — crash the wave and ping his vault path.

edits.before: That’s Talon’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Post-items his 575 leap kills you outright — peel your carry, don't hunt.

edits.before: Spending Mantra on wave-clear while behind on poke — Karma without RQ banked is a support who took mid's farm.
edits.after: With your E shield down, one Noxian Diplomacy plus a Rake return is your health bar — hold the wave until it returns.

edits.before: Talon needs wall proximity to threaten his E-vault burst combo; poke him from open lane and he has no way to punish without overextending into your range.
edits.after: Talon's burst needs no wall — Noxian Diplomacy leaps from 575 and Rake reaches 650. Poke from your full 950 and never let him inside that gap without W up.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 you outrange him and he has no answer to poke since his combo needs terrain to function, so push the CS and HP lead hard while staying off walls. This continues through levels 3-5 as his damage is still mana-light but positionally dependent, letting you freely punish any overextension near brush or terrain.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 you outrange him 950 to 650 and he cannot answer poke without walking into your Q, so push the CS and HP lead hard. This continues through levels 3-5: Noxian Diplomacy is 8s at rank 1 and only reaches 575, so punish every step he takes toward the wave and keep W banked for the leap rather than spending it on minions.

edits.before: Set up near walls to threaten vault-stun burst combos
edits.after: Vault a wall, open with Rake, then leap in with Q
